# Pyloxa

> Pyloxa is a desktop app for Windows 10 and 11 that gets AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex CLI to work together on one software project. You describe the work once; Pyloxa plans it, hands each task to an agent by your routing rules, checks the result with your own verification commands, and leaves the merge to you. It runs the official CLIs on your own subscriptions or API keys and does not resell or proxy any AI service. The free edition is a direct download.

## The name

Pyloxa is made from the first letters of Plan, Yield, Lead, Orchestrate, eXecute and Agents: the brain plans the work, yields only results that pass your checks, leads the agents by your rules, orchestrates Claude Code and Codex, executes each task in its own git worktree, and works with the agents you already use.

## Key facts

- Platform: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit. Requires git and at least one signed-in Claude Code or Codex CLI. A setup wizard checks git and Node.js and installs the CLIs with their official npm commands after you confirm.
- Agents: Claude Code and Codex CLI. Gemini CLI is experimental support and needs your own paid Gemini API key; it cannot be the brain or test other agents' work.
- How it works: a "brain" agent reads the project and writes a plan. Each task goes to a CLI by routing rules you write (for example "backend tasks go to Codex"), runs in its own git worktree on its own branch, and is checked against the write scope in the plan and your verification commands (for example `npm run test`). You can also have a different agent test the work. You accept results and decide what is merged and pushed.
- Workflow: one page shows the whole flow in five steps (plan, phases, assignment, checks, delivery), with an assignment table of task types by agent and five built-in templates (Balanced, Quick fix, Thorough review, Share the quota, Spec first). The brain lays out the phases, or you define up to five stages yourself: who does each one, whether it waits for your approval, and whether it can be skipped.
- Verification card: a PR description can carry a verification card with one table per phase (who did the work, who cross-tested it, which commands Pyloxa ran, how each result was accepted). An agent reporting "done" never counts as passing. An optional closing line says "Verified with Pyloxa" only when every result passed the commands Pyloxa ran; otherwise it says "Verification record by Pyloxa". The same card can be opened in the app when a plan finishes.
- Test drive: the setup wizard can create a small shopping-cart sample repo with a hidden rounding bug and a plan written in advance. One agent builds a feature, Pyloxa runs `node --test` itself, and an agent from another vendor cross-tests (automatically in Pro, on request in the free edition); with only one agent, a spec test in the repo does the checking. It needs git and Node.js, shows an estimate of agent turns, tokens and time first, and never touches your projects, pushes or opens a PR.
- Moving to a new PC: Settings → Backup and transfer exports agent profiles, global routing rules, preferences, stages, prompt templates, global shared memory, the skills library and interface preferences to one file, and imports it with a per-item preview and an automatic backup first. API keys, sign-ins, licenses, machine paths and per-project settings are never included.
- When quota runs out: Pyloxa stops sending work to that CLI, shows when the quota resets, and proposes a fallback from your rules. After you confirm, the other CLI continues from the files already changed. At most 3 automatic attempts and 2 fallback takeovers per task; no API charges you have not approved.
- Background: closing the window while work runs keeps Pyloxa in the system tray; interrupted work can be resumed.
- Credentials and privacy: Pyloxa never reads, copies or sends CLI tokens or credential files, and never stashes or resets your working directory. It never sends your code or prompts to us; your code goes only where each CLI already sends it. The free edition needs no account. The trial, the Pro preview and Pro use a sign-in account only for licensing, with a license refresh about once a day that sends a device ID and the app and Windows versions to account.pyloxa.com. Anonymous usage statistics (counts and categories only) are sent only if you turn them on, and they are off by default. It checks GitHub for updates and the CLI compatibility catalog, which can be turned off.
- Installer: not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run.
- Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, OpenAI or Google.

## Free and Pro

- Free (US$0, no account): one project working at a time, routing rules, the workflow page with five templates and your own stages, verification commands, phase gates, brain review, cross-testing on request, verification cards, fallback proposals you confirm, desktop notifications, an inventory of the skills each CLI can see, the test drive, and settings export and import. The free edition stays free.
- Pro (US$79 a year; early bird US$49 a year, unchanged for as long as you stay subscribed), in a free preview since 0.1.10: sign in to use every Pro feature until Pro goes on sale, with at least 30 days’ notice, then 14 more days of Pro. Pro adds several projects at once with one task center, automatic decisions within limits you set (auto mode), an automatic fallback chain, automatic cross-testing with failed tests sent back for a fix, a backup brain, project priority, per-connection quotas and scheduled plans, a usage dashboard with Markdown/CSV reports, notifications to Telegram, Discord or a webhook, a skills library synced to every CLI with per-project or per-profile assignment, dispatch packs, saved workflows with a different one per project, workflows drafted by the brain from one sentence (shown as a diff before you apply or save them), and Agent Teams (experimental). If you stop paying, Pro keeps working on versions released while you paid.
